clue.text: Money used for bribing men to clear snow away?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what pays the gang who shovel snow, and the word bribe hangs in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a fund that pays for slush (melting snow) to be cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret pot of cash kept for illicit payments is the standard phrase; read literally it is money set aside for wet snow.

clue.text: Ghastly old city breaking cover

indicators.note: one piece breaking another means it splits it open and sits inside

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Something horrid about an ancient city whose disguise is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid and ghastly both describe something shocking and gruesome.

clue.text: It could be the belief that sustains a Japanese, not his ruin

definitions.text: the belief that sustains a Japanese

indicators.note: ruin tells us the letters of the words not his are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A remark that faith keeps a Japanese person going rather than bringing his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' turns NOTHIS into the answer; 'It could be' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native religion of Japan.

clue.text: An impertinent aviator credulously thought to come from a world other than ours?

definitions.text: An impertinent aviator credulously thought to come from a world other than ours?

parts.words: An impertinent aviator credulously thought to come from a world other than ours?
parts.note: a saucy thing that flies, which credulous people believe is an alien craft

explanation.surface: A cheeky pilot whom gullible people think is from another planet.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue covers 4 and 23 together. A saucer is an old word for a cheeky person, and the flying sort is the disc-shaped craft of UFO stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The disc-shaped alien spacecraft of popular belief carries this two-word name.

clue.text: Approaches an auditor in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: one piece in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province of Nova Scotia
an auditor is a listener, and an ear does the listening

explanation.surface: Someone approaches an accountant on a trip to Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer: the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to approach it.

clue.text: A mount from which a fiery outburst may from time to time be expected

definitions.text: A mount from which a fiery outburst may from time to time be expected

parts.words: A mount from which a fiery outburst may from time to time be expected
parts.note: a mountain liable to erupt, phrased like a hot-tempered person or a horse

explanation.surface: A steed with a temper that flares up now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain that still erupts now and again is the geological term described.

clue.text: A tense forecast of idyllic days to come

definitions.text: forecast of idyllic days to come

explanation.surface: A strained prediction of blissful times ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous; it is the grammatical tense, as in 'will have done'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar tense for actions completed by a later time; read literally, a promise that times ahead will be ideal.

clue.text: Rarely does one come across anything that has it

definitions.text: Rarely does one come across anything that has it

parts.words: Rarely does one come across anything that has it
parts.note: worth that comes from being rare: anything with it is seldom met

explanation.surface: A remark that you hardly ever find something with this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth that an item gains purely from being rare is the economic term.

clue.text: Method used by educationists for sorting out new emigrants

definitions.text: Method used by educationists for sorting out

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of emigrants are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: Teachers sort out newly arrived emigrants by some method.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouping pupils into classes by ability is the schools' practice of that name.

clue.text: The person who should get the post eventually

definitions.text: The person who should get the post eventually

parts.words: The person who should get the post eventually
parts.note: the one a letter is sent to, phrased like someone in line for a job

explanation.surface: Someone destined to win a job in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The one named on an envelope is the intended recipient of mail.

clue.text: Had a shot at being a judge?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to have a go at being a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot is to attempt; a judge hears a case, so a judged case has been heard in court.

clue.text: Healthy noise

explanation.definitionFit: Healthy as in 'of sound mind'; a noise is anything heard.

clue.text: Not a good way to make money

definitions.text: Not a good way to make money

parts.words: Not a good way to make money
parts.note: making money literally, by counterfeiting it, which is criminal

explanation.surface: A warning about an unprofitable line of business.
explanation.definitionFit: To fake banknotes or coins is to counterfeit, a crime rather than a career.

clue.text: Doting on a man such as Henry or Peter

definitions.text: man such as Henry or Peter

parts.note: doting on someone is being fond of them

explanation.surface: Someone dotes on a man called Henry or Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry and Peter are members of the American acting family.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry and his son Peter are actors of the Fonda family.

clue.text: Is taking a hundred gunners round a place in Gwent

indicators.note: one piece round another means it surrounds it

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Artillerymen surround somewhere in a Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' here means adding on at the end, not containing. Gwent is a county in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Risca is a town in the Welsh county of Gwent.

clue.text: Celt torn apart by a conspicuous success

indicators.note: torn apart tells us the letters of Celt are pulled out of order

explanation.surface: A Celtic warrior ripped apart in a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn apart' rearranges CELT to ECLT, and 'by a' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant, showy success.

clue.text: Still rings back, nevertheless

parts.note: still, as in 'still better', means even

indicators.note: back tells us the letters for rings are read in the other direction

parts.note: rings are round like the letter O, so OS

explanation.surface: Someone keeps ringing back regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases concede a point and carry on: all the same.

clue.text: He is entitled to a share of whatever is left

definitions.text: He is entitled to a share of whatever is left

parts.words: He is entitled to a share of whatever is left
parts.note: one heir among several splitting an estate, phrased like a scavenger for leftovers

explanation.surface: Someone claiming part of the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint heir shares an inheritance with others.

clue.text: Alan's queer American accent?

indicators.note: queer in its old sense of odd tells us the letters are made strange

parts.note: the name with its S

explanation.surface: A man named Alan has an odd American way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' (odd) rearranges ALANS. The question mark flags that the twang is a typical, not universal, US accent.
explanation.definitionFit: US speech is often said to have a nasal twang, sounded through the nose.

clue.text: State of mind in which Engineers are not able to sail?

indicators.note: in which places one piece within the other

parts.note: a mood is a state of mind
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

explanation.surface: A frame of mind in which army engineers cannot go sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not able to sail' describes a boat tied up, not a person; the surface makes the engineers seem stuck in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat tied up at its berth cannot sail off.

clue.text: Office counters best given a wide berth!

explanation.surface: Office equipment that, oddly, should be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the snake, Britain's venomous viper, best avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding machines count figures in an office; vipers are snakes to steer clear of.

clue.text: A huge shipping order to hold to

parts.note: vast means huge

explanation.surface: A vast vessel is ordered to stand still.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a sailor's command to stop or hold.

clue.text: Type of dance the Spanish and French hold in Virginia

indicators.note: the words hold in mean the pieces are held inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
el is Spanish for the
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Spanish and French people stage a dance in Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A veleta is an old-time ballroom dance in waltz time.

clue.text: See 4

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'See 4': the puzzle file has no group linking it to 4-down, so the shared clue (FLYING SAUCER) is annotated on 4-down alone

clue.text: 25's razor cuts?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether shaving cuts belong to the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SATAN, nicknamed Old Nick, so the devil's are Nick's; small cuts when shaving are nicks.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is called Old Nick, giving a possessive; shaving cuts are small nicks.

clue.text: The enemy Sally Ann has to beat!

explanation.surface: The foe the Salvation Army must defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally Ann' is British slang for the Salvation Army, a Christian charity which fights the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is the arch-enemy, and the Salvation Army's whole mission is to defeat him.

clue.text: Silly mistake made in showing affection

indicators.note: made in means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An embarrassing blunder in a display of fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder.

clue.text: The degree to which Edgar could change

indicators.note: could change tells us the letters of Edgar can be altered in order

explanation.surface: How far a man named Edgar might alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a level or degree on a scale.

clue.text: Troubled throne taking a risk about an opportunity to make amends

indicators.note: troubled tells us the letters of throne are disturbed

parts.note: a chance is a risk

explanation.surface: An uneasy monarch gambles to make up for past wrongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' rearranges the six letters of the throne; 'taking a' fixes A to the front, and 'about' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A second go lets someone put right an earlier failure.

clue.text: Singularly ill equipped to understand union troubles?

definitions.text: Singularly ill equipped to understand union troubles?

parts.words: Singularly ill equipped to understand union troubles?
parts.note: someone single, never married, cannot grasp marital strife

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is unusually bad at grasping trade-union disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being single, with no spouse, means no direct experience of wedlock.
